question: Should an empty QA Lab dashboard or `/api/scenario/suite` request retain the existing live, fast, flow-only behavior, or intentionally switch to the new canonical `smoke-ci` profile defaults?
rationale: Both paths are technically coherent, but they intentionally produce different provider, scenario, channel-driver, evidence, and fast-mode results for existing operator automation; repository policy treats changed defaults and fallback removal as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Preserve empty-request compatibility
options.body: Keep the old dashboard/API defaults for omitted selections and make `smoke-ci` behavior explicit through the profile control or a documented opt-in request.

options.title: Approve the canonical smoke default
options.body: Accept `smoke-ci` as the new empty-request contract and require explicit maintainer sign-off plus clear operator-facing documentation of the changed run characteristics.

recommendation.title: Preserve empty-request compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep the old dashboard/API defaults for omitted selections and make `smoke-ci` behavior explicit through the profile control or a documented opt-in request.
